milestones.title: Jesuits found the college of São Paulo
milestones.detail: On 25 January 1554 Jesuit priests founded a college to catechise the indigenous peoples; the settlement of São Paulo dos Campos de Piratininga grew around it.

milestones.title: Settlement raised to a vila
milestones.detail: By order of governor-general Mem de Sá the inhabitants of Santo André da Borda do Campo were moved to the college, and the settlement became the Vila de São Paulo with its own municipal chamber.

milestones.title: Seat of the Captaincy of São Vicente
milestones.detail: On 22 March 1681 the donee of the Captaincy of São Vicente moved its capital to São Paulo, naming it head of the captaincy.

milestones.title: Elevated to city status
milestones.detail: On 11 July 1711 the town of São Paulo was elevated to the status of city.

milestones.title: Brazil's independence proclaimed at Ipiranga
milestones.detail: On 7 September 1822 Pedro I is held to have proclaimed Brazil's independence on the banks of the Ipiranga stream in São Paulo; the Monument to Independence was inaugurated on the site in 1922.

milestones.title: São Paulo Railway opens
milestones.detail: The São Paulo Railway from the port of Santos began operating on 16 February 1867, the day the first Luz station opened; it was later known as the Santos-Jundiaí line.

milestones.title: Avenida Paulista inaugurated
milestones.detail: Paulista Avenue was inaugurated on 8 December 1891; it began as a residential thoroughfare flanked by ornate mansions.

milestones.title: Population nearly quadruples in a decade
milestones.detail: The census counted 239,820 people, up from 64,934 in 1890, as coffee wealth and mass immigration transformed the town into a metropolis.
milestones.source: Prefeitura de São Paulo, SMUL/GEOINFO, 'População: Brasil, Estado de São Paulo, RM de São Paulo e Município de São Paulo, 1872-2022' (IBGE censuses), https://drive.prefeitura.sp.gov.br/cidade/secretarias/upload/chamadas/312_censo_br-rm-uf-msp_pop-abs_1872-2022_final_1715804954.htm

milestones.title: Revolt and bombardment of the city
milestones.detail: During the 23-day São Paulo Revolt of July 1924 federal forces shelled the city; about a third of its roughly 700,000 inhabitants fled.

milestones.title: Prestes Maia's Avenues Plan presented
milestones.detail: Francisco Prestes Maia published the Plano de Avenidas para a Cidade de São Paulo (1930), a plan for large avenues connecting the centre with the outskirts that overhauled the city's traffic.
milestones.source: Prestes Maia, Plano de Avenidas para a Cidade de São Paulo (Melhoramentos, 1930), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo

milestones.title: Fourth centenary: Ibirapuera Park and the cathedral
milestones.detail: For the city's 400th anniversary Ibirapuera Park was created and the new Sé Cathedral was consecrated.

milestones.title: Overtakes Rio as Brazil's largest city
milestones.detail: In the 1960 census São Paulo (3,781,446) surpassed Rio de Janeiro as the most populous city in Brazil.
milestones.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo; Prefeitura de São Paulo, SMUL/GEOINFO, 'População: Brasil, Estado de São Paulo, RM de São Paulo e Município de São Paulo, 1872-2022' (IBGE censuses), https://drive.prefeitura.sp.gov.br/cidade/secretarias/upload/chamadas/312_censo_br-rm-uf-msp_pop-abs_1872-2022_final_1715804954.htm

milestones.title: Metropolitan Region of São Paulo created
milestones.detail: The Região Metropolitana de São Paulo was created in 1973, grouping the municipality with its neighbours.
milestones.source: Prefeitura de São Paulo, SMUL/GEOINFO, 'População: Brasil, Estado de São Paulo, RM de São Paulo e Município de São Paulo, 1872-2022' (IBGE censuses), https://drive.prefeitura.sp.gov.br/cidade/secretarias/upload/chamadas/312_censo_br-rm-uf-msp_pop-abs_1872-2022_final_1715804954.htm

milestones.title: Metro begins operating
milestones.detail: Construction of the metro began in 1968 and commercial operation of the first line started on 14 September 1974.

milestones.title: Octávio Frias de Oliveira Bridge opens
milestones.detail: The cable-stayed bridge over the Pinheiros river, with a 138 m mast carrying two curved decks, was inaugurated on 10 May 2008 after three years of construction.

landmarks.name: Obelisk of São Paulo (Ibirapuera)
landmarks.source: Condephaat, Mausoléu do Soldado Constitucionalista, http://condephaat.sp.gov.br/benstombados/mausoleu-do-soldado-constitucionalista-2/ via https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obelisco_de_S%C3%A3o_Paulo

notes: Start date: the Jesuit college founded on 25 January 1554 is the documented founding and is not contested; the Tupiniquim village of Piratininga that preceded it is not counted as the city. Population: no figure before 1836 could be sourced in this session. The colonial household lists of 1765 and 1798 exist (Marcílio, A cidade de São Paulo: povoamento e população, 1750-1850) but their city totals were not seen on an open page, so the series is empty for 1554-1835. The 1836 and 1854 counts cover the whole 'termo' including rural parishes later split off as separate municipalities (Cotia, Guarulhos, Juqueri, São Bernardo), so they overstate the town itself and are not strictly comparable with 1886 (seven parishes) or with the IBGE censuses from 1872 (Município de São Paulo, population present). English Wikipedia's timeline also lists 130,775 for an 1893 count without a citation; it is left out. The 1940 figure is the Prefeitura's (1,318,539, preliminary synopsis); the commonly quoted final figure is 1,326,261. Landmarks: modern tower heights and completion years are from CTBUH (which dates the Martinelli building to 1934, although it was inaugurated in 1929 and extended later). The Obelisk was inaugurated in 1955 though works are reported to have concluded only in 1970; 1955 is used. The cathedral was consecrated in 1954 and its towers completed in 1967; 1967 is used with the 92 m tower height. Left out for lack of a sourced height: the colonial and 19th-century monuments (Pátio do Colégio church, Mosteiro de São Bento, Igreja de São Francisco, Luz Station clock tower, Theatro Municipal, Museu do Ipiranga, Monument to Independence), so nothing before 1924 is represented. Milestones rely mainly on Wikipedia articles and the Prefeitura census table.
